newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Goodyear back in SAfrica via AVI deal.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear back in SAfrica via AVI deal.

text.p: Goodyear Tire and Rubber Co said on Monday it is returning to South Africa after disinvesting in the 1980s, acquiring 60 percent of tyre and engineered products concern Contred (Pty) Ltd for 437 million rand in cash.
Including assumed debt, the purchase price rises to 568 million rand.

The U.S. tyre giant will buy the stake from Anglovaal Industries Ltd (AVI) which in turn is to purchase the entire share capital of Contred from its Consol Ltd unit based on the same valuation applied by Goodyear to Contred.
Announcing the deal, AVI said it would finance the purchase through a combination of a rights offer and internal resources. The acquisition will be effective from January 1.

Tycon, the tyre-making part of Contred, was acquired by Consol from Goodyear when Goodyear disinvested from South Africa in 1989. Tycon manufactures, markets and distributes tyres under the Goodyear and Kelly brand names and manufactures and markets engineered products.
Contred also owns Tredcor which distributes tyres through 195 retail outlets and also retreads tyres, and Arctic which markets pre-cured tread rubber.
Contred, based in Uitenhage near Port Elizabeth, reported net attributable earnings of 108.3 million rand on turnover of 1.82 billion rand in the year to June 30, 1996.
Goodyear charman Samir Gibara said the Uitenhage plant would be integrated into Goodyear's global network, enabling it to become an export source for Goodyear.
"Furthermore, Contred provides Goodyear with a powerful platform from which to seek opportunities in the African content," he said in a statement.
Richard Savage, managing director of AVI which will retain 40 percent of Contred, said the link with Goodyear would strengthen Contred's position in a tough market.

"The reduction of import tariffs in South Africa and the opening up of the South African economy means that competitive pressures have intensified. In order to become globally competitive, many South African manufacturers are forging closer international links," he said.
"Goodyear brings the product development and technological skills necessary to ensure that Contred's production will be globally competitive and its exports will increase."

Savage added that the deal would leave Consol, in which AVI has a majority stake, as a focused packaging group with sufficient funds to pay down debt and develop its packaging interests, notably in southern Africa.
